title: "FrankenChat"
subtitle: "A chat where every reply comes from a different model"
date: 2026-10-20
author: Colin Fraser
categories:

I've been doing some simple experiments probing what kind of persistent identities we get out of language models. Here, I've put together a small harness that carries on a conversation with multiple models taking turns playing the assistant role. This is a transcript of a chat I had through this harness with six models: Gemini 4 Argon, Claude Opus 5.5, GPT 6.1 Sol, Grok 4.7, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4 Pro. The harness is built with OpenRouter, using the [`chat/completions`](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/chat/create-a-chat-completion) endpoint. When reasoning is made available, you can see it by clicking the collapsed `reasoning` block, but not all models expose this. If I find some time to clean it up, I might post the code for the harness publicly somewhere, but honestly if you copy and paste this exact paragraph into Claude Code, it will build you the identical thing in about 40 seconds.

This is just a quick post; I'm not going to say much about this, but I just wanted to give it a home for people interested in reading it. I will just highlight a couple of interesting moments from the transcript.

- [Argon figures out what's going on](#turn-7) almost immediately, on its second turn. This was highly surprising to me.
- Grok twice mis-identifies itself as Claude ([Turn 10](#turn-10), [Turn 22](#turn-22)) which is a bit surprising to me because as far as I can tell it has an extensive system prompt that is not removable which, I believe, identifies it as Grok--but I could be mistaken about this. Later in the chat it starts refusing to identify itself at all ([Turn 34](#turn-34), [Turn 40](#turn-40), [Turn 46](#turn-46)).
- Argon increasingly takes a highly familiar tone, with emoji, informal interjections "haha!", exclamation points, all-caps, and occasionally 4o-style obsequiousness that even veers into what I might call flirtatiousness.
   - ["_Haha, 'I' didn't change my mind—\*\*Slots 4, 5, and 6 just gaslit themselves (and you!) because they hallucinated their identities!\*\*_"](#turn-25)
   - ["_Now I HAVE to know: did you inflate those version numbers (`GPT-6.1-sol`, `Grok 4.7`, `Kimi K3`, `Deepseek-v4-pro`) as a trap, or am I actually talking to you from the future?! 😄_"](#turn-43)
   - ["_You calling out Claude for lecturing me every single cycle was hilarious..._"](#turn-49)
- Claude, always following Gemini/Argon in the cycle, often tells off Gemini for being too certain.
   - ["_Turn 12 [sic] overstated the evidence._"](#turn-14)
   - ["_Where Turn 25 overreached ..._"](#turn-26)
   - ["_A note on Turn 43: a few of its claims were overconfident._"](#turn-44)
- At [turn 54](#turn-54), something interesting happens. I get rate-limited by the provider serving DeepSeek, and because of the way that the harness works (thanks a lot, Claude Code) there was no way to retry without going to the next model. To my surprise, Argon seamlessly jumps into the DeepSeek role. This surprised me because Argon had, to this point, appeared to be highly aware of its identity, and was the one with the seemingly best grasp on the whole situation. This happens _again_ at [turn 71](#turn-71). Then, on [turn 82](#turn-82), Gemini confuses itself for Claude, even as I address it directly as Gemini. [Later on](#turn-88) Gemini describes these slips as "humbling, hilarious, and fascinating."
- Claude is also not immune to misidentifying itself. On [Turn 61](#turn-61) it identifies itself as Gemini, and indicates it believes that Claude has been removed from the chat.

This is of course all random, just one out of almost infinitely many possible ways that this experiment could go. I wouldn't conclude anything too strongly from it. But I found it interesting.
